name: An installation can accept bound keys only
aliases: an authorized_keys line without a project or a principal is refused
summary: One installation setting: deployment.private.json's bound_keys_only, absent or false meaning off, so nothing changes where nothing is configured. admin.py bound-keys-only status|on|off --actor OPERATOR is operator-gated, holds the deployment config lock, writes nothing when nothing changes, and appends an audit entry to bound_keys_only_audit, a damaged list kept aside as bound_keys_only_audit_damaged_<stamp>. With it on, ssh_forced_command.py reads the runtime's own settings file and refuses, before selecting or running anything, a line naming no --project or no --principal: exit status 2, the missing part named, nothing run; a line naming both is launched as before. A settings file that cannot be read refuses every forced-command key, naming the file; a value that is neither true nor false reads as off with a warning. setup-status reports a bound_keys_only block (enabled true/false/null with a sentence); authorized-keys refuses to print a line the setting would refuse (--role operator unaffected); authorized-keys-list reports the setting and flags such lines. A line printed before an upgrade runs another release's wrapper, which knows nothing of it; an older kit ignores the key.
